technical_and_design_decisions: The library will be implemented in Go, consistent with the Hyperledger Fabric ecosystem's primary implementation language.

Existing Hyperledger Fabric protobuf definitions (from the fabric-protos-go package) and base config parsing/ConfigUpdate generation logic from the existing fabric-config library will be reused, with no reimplementation of core config handling required.
All new public functions will follow existing naming and signature conventions of the fabric-config package to ensure idiomatic usage for existing Fabric developers.

Certificate validation for the add root CA function (U4) will use the standard Go crypto/x509 package to check for the KeyUsageCertSign flag and CA:TRUE basic constraint, with no full certificate chain validation performed per the minimal validation requirement in the acceptance criteria.
Helper functions for retrieving anchor peers (U7) and orderer configuration (U8) will return strongly typed Go structs instead of raw protobuf messages to simplify usage for library consumers.
All usage examples will be added as runnable Go examples in the package source code, so they are automatically included in generated GoDoc documentation.
Unit tests will use existing Hyperledger Fabric test config fixtures (sample channel configs, MSP configs, test certificates) to ensure consistency with existing test suites.
assumptions: The existing base fabric-config library (including config block parsing, ConfigUpdate envelope generation, and signing workflow utilities) is already implemented and available for use, so no effort is required to build these core components.
The development environment has all required Hyperledger Fabric dependencies (fabric-protos-go, fabric-config, test fixtures) already installed and configured.

The input configuration (config block or transaction) provided to all functions is a valid, well-formed Fabric channel configuration, per the acceptance criteria's premise of starting with an existing valid config.

For the certificate revocation function (U3), the input certificate is confirmed to be issued by the target MSP, so no additional validation of the certificate's issuer is required per the acceptance criteria's scope.
For the add root CA function (U4), duplicate certificate checks only need to compare the raw DER bytes of the certificate, with no additional metadata comparison required.
The existing test network used for integration testing is already provisioned and accessible, so no effort is required to set up the underlying Fabric network infrastructure.
